full_judgment: 16. Now we are going to consider the title of the parties. Plaintiff 14 who was one of the executants of Exhibit-Uma dated 5-5-1991 has deposed as PW 1. Although Exhibit-Uma is a deed of relinquishment and the same does not confer title but it is a registered document of admission and since no relief was prayed against Exhibits-Uma and Cha the documents stand good and plaintiff 14 is bound by such admission made in Exhibit-Uma and he is estopped from denying such admission thus the value of his testimony is greatly diminished. PW 2 and PW 3 deposed on possession and PW 3 failed to corroborate PW 2 as he admitted in cross that the land of Abdur Rahman is enjoyed by his sons. However since this is mainly a suit for partition evidence on possession does not carry much value except title. Plaintiffs claim title through settlement from auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin. But they did not file any document of such settlement. It was not also explained away by them as to why they could not put forth such document. The document of title of the defendants for the selfsame land has been validated in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants claim title through settlement from Hachen and others by registered dakhila Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946. It appears from the pleadings and evidence that plaintiffs have relied on RS record 487 Exhibit-IX as the basis of their claim. Record of right is not a document of title. Moreover this Exhibit-IX has lost its value' by virtue of the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and the judgment passed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants on the strength of decree mutated their names by Exhibit-Jha series and have been maintaining possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Jha series. Earlier respondents filed three applications for amendment of the plaint and for taking additional evidence along with a supplementary affidavit but according to the order dated 30-11-2017 passed by a bench of this Court respondents did not press those applications at the time of hearing. So those applications are rejected being not pressed. Respondents also filed another application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and also for acceptance of additional evidence on 30-3-2023 and those applications were heard. In the amendment of plaint respondents have made out a new case of kabuliyat and dakhila and in its support filed certified copies of kabuliyat and dakhila through application for acceptance of additional evidence. We have carefully examined those two documents and it appears that the kabuliyat dated 17-8-1944 was accepted by Hachen and others and they granted a dakhila on the same day to Rahman and his brothers. The second auction as drawn in the original plaint has been disowned in this amendment. Earlier plaintiffs claimed through Gogon and Mofijuddin and the rent was 50 taka 6 anna and quantum of the holding was 9.72 acres according to schedule-Ka. Now they are claiming through Hachen and others and the joma is 44 taka 8 anna and quantum of joma is 8.75 acres which is inconsistent with schedule-Ka. The dakhila shows that education cess is fixed at 2 taka 4 anna which actually was not imposed at the time in 1351 BS as found our Appellate Division in the case of Joynal Abedin Molla vs Aliyar Rahman and others, 1983 BLD (AD) 105. Plaintiffs were acquainted with Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946 since 1978 when Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 was filed. That document stands good in the suit and revision Exhibit-Kha series, Ga and Gha. Now after around 26(twenty-six) years plaintiffs have come forward with those applications in view to fill up their lacuna by making out a new case on their acquisition of title to the surprise of the other party. The other party cannot be taken by surprise specially when a valuable right is accrued in their favour by lapse of time. Had Exhibit-Kha series been found fraudulent according to pleading and evidence in that case these proposed applications would have been taken in adjudication. It also calls for our attention that in Title Suit 126 of 1983 the RS tenants Gani Faraji, Abul Khaleque, Tofayel Ahmed admitting the title of Rahman Faraji which he acquired through Exhibit-Ka entered into compromise which was not denied in revision Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Court has to follow the principles of law and we have no option but to reject those applications filed after such a belated stage. It has also come to our notice that in paragraph 2 of the application for production of additional evidence it is admitted that the original kabulyat was under the custody of executant Abdur Rahman Faraji thus it appears that the same was not acted upon being not accepted by the landlord.
